pr.title: Use VNNI K layout in AMX attention
pr.head: 0ee8671d35

short_version: PR 2 (#4887) adds qk_vnni_128x4, an AMX kernel that scores one query group against one dense page by reading the VNNI-packed K plane of PR 1 in place, and it removes PR 1's temporary gate that kept such pages off the dense AMX page path.

The page introduces two data models (the padded query rows and the typed K view the kernel takes) and one algorithm (the kernel's four-step tile loop), carried by the core diagrams K_VNNI-B2 (the type model) and KV_CACHE-B3 (the function model) and by the context diagram K_VNNI-B1 (the plane).
The shared block save of PR 3, the two bit arrays of the page and the row-major tail block of PR 4 are not in this PR, and the diagrams that draw them are marked context or not involved.

words.definition: The first and the second matrix of one AMX tile multiply: the multiply accepts a row-major matrix only as A and needs the VNNI layout for B. For qk_vnni_128x4 the padded query rows are A and the 16 K panels of the page are B, and for qk_rowmajor_128x4 the native K page is A and the VNNI-packed queries are B.
Tile registers 0 to 3 of the AMX kernels, into which the tile multiply adds its products, so they hold the running sums. In qk_vnni_128x4 accumulator tile b holds the scores of token block b.
Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS consumes the VNNI layout as its B operand, and one 1 KiB panel is exactly one B tile.
The CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels and the code that selects them. Without it the AMX tests are placeholder cases and every page takes the software path.

The function of self_attention.hpp that applies one dense page to one query with the AMX QK kernel and the AMX PV kernel in one call. In this PR it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with page::k_packed under the layout gate and qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k otherwise [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1749, 1781-1787].

The per-page scoring function of self_attention.hpp. For one (query, page) pair it takes the dense AMX page path when the compile-time and run-time conditions hold, and otherwise scores the page with the reader qk_group (VNNI slot) or the dotter (row-major slot) [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1856, 1904-1910, 1994-1997].
The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer, which read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted the latch down and never write K. The kernel of this PR runs on them.
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set, with 16 lanes of 32 bits per register. The reader qk_group is AVX-512 code with one token per lane.
bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values and of the queries the packers copy. fp32 (32-bit float) is the accumulation format of the score kernels.

16 consecutive tokens of a page, page offsets 16 c to 16 c + 15, c = 0 to 3 (k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16, TOKEN_BLOCKS_4), whose bytes are its 4 panels (one per dimension step, 4 KiB in all). In this PR every block of a VNNI slot holds the VNNI form.

PR 4's per-slot record of which 16-token blocks of a page hold the VNNI form: one bit per block in the atomic byte k_vnni_blocks_, read by page::k_vnni_blocks with acquire order. It does not exist at this PR.
PR 4's in-place conversions of one 16-token block between the row-major form and the VNNI form (h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp at PR 4). Not in this PR.

The unit of KV memory allocation of tron: it reserves space for a number of pages, owns that memory and hands out pages. Its public methods and the page's are the interface of kv_cache.hpp [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:832].

clear_kv_complete_at is the main-branch page function that resets a page offset when a new token takes it, and k_forget_row is PR 4's addition that drops the K bits of that offset and above [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2185]. Both run between forward passes under the tree lock.

PR 4's forward-end conversion: save_k queues each block that a short run completed in pending_k_blocks_, and convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks after wait_for_coop_gof. Not in this PR.

copy_from copies a token range of every slot from another page (main-branch code) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2322], and copy_storage_slot does it for one storage slot. PR 1 made a whole-page copy one owner assignment and a smaller range a token-by-token copy_token (load_row then store_row) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2280, 2296, 2298-2301; h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:334-341].
Prefill is the phase that scores the prompt tokens of a request, and its wall time is the TTFT. Decode is the generation phase where every step saves one token per user, and its rate is the TPS.

words.term: dense page / dense AMX page path
words.definition: A dense page is a full 64-token page that the query sees whole and inside its sliding window (the span of past tokens the model attends to), checked by is_dense_amx_page. The dense AMX page path applies such a page with the AMX QK and PV kernels, under the compile-time condition amx_attn_h128g4::eligible and the run-time conditions of a packed query (amx_q_packed != nullptr) and is_dense_amx_page [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1904-1910].

A dimension step is 32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (k_vnni::STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16), the depth of one AMX tile multiply, so a 128-dimension head has 4 steps. A pair is two adjacent dimensions of one token stored in one 32-bit dword.

The test that checks routing with stand-in kernels that count their calls instead of running AMX. In this PR the fakes of both packers and both QK kernels count into one probe, the VNNI packer's fake also counts into its own counter (rows_pack_calls), and the test checks that the packer of the build's layout ran [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63, 171, 196, 260-274].

The per-token dot-product loop of self_attention.hpp (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp), which scores row-major K one token per call. In this PR it is compiled only for row-major slots (PR 4 lets it score the rows of a row-major tail block).
The extra physical slot of a book for the EAGLE speculation model (main-branch code). PR 4 gives it its own entry in the page's K-state arrays.

amx_attn_h128g4::eligible is the compile-time gate of the AMX path: head size 128, kv_mul 4 and a bf16 query type [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:170-171]. is_dense_amx_page is the run-time check that a page is dense for one query [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1725].

book::fill_random is the test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values, and fill_storage_slot is its body for one storage slot. PR 1 made it reach a VNNI plane through k_vnni_access::plane, the one documented exception to the typed access rule [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1290, 1715, 1721].

A run that feeds every binary a fixed token sequence through --force-feed-text-token-file, so all binaries score the same context at every step. The PR body uses one to show that this binary with the kill switch and PR 1's binary score identically at all 256 steps.

The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof returned [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1834, 1838]. Nothing runs there in this PR, and PR 4 converts the queued blocks there.

The FPGA (field-programmable gate array) is the card that scores attention in hardware, and cached_operation_uses_hw says once per model whether an operation's K is scored there [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1529]. This PR has no hardware-attention policy (PR 4 keeps the blocks of such operations row-major).

words.term: GOF staging gather (gof::populate, k_head_fn, help_drain_gof, wait_for_coop_gof)
words.definition: A GOF is a group of four tokens of K/V data that gof::populate copies into a buffer for the FPGA [src/tron/gof.cpp:188], and page_info::k_head_fn returns one token's K row for it, since PR 1 through page::get_k_row from a VNNI plane [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2759]. Idle attention workers run the staging through help_drain_gof and the main thread drains the rest in wait_for_coop_gof [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3239, 3252].

The case "AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K" of t_amx_numerics, which returns early with a warning without AMX hardware [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:219-279]. It stores the same K row-major and, through store_row in scrambled token order, VNNI-packed, packs the same queries both ways, runs both kernels on real AMX and compares the 4 x 64 fp32 scores bit for bit for 2 seeds.

PR 3's protocol in which the main thread cuts a minibatch into work units (k_store_cut_units), opens a window (opened), every thread of the window claims units (next_unit) and stores them with store_k_block, the helpers leave (finished) and main joins under a watchdog (k_join_clock_spins). k_store_shared decides whether a store is shared. worker_ix and n_workers name the threads. Not in this PR.
PR 4's third condition of the dense AMX page path: page::k_vnni_blocks must say that all 4 blocks of the page are VNNI. In this PR the path has two run-time conditions only.

The read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane for a slot and KV head, VNNI slots only [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997-2001]. In this PR it is the argument of both score kernels: qk_vnni_128x4 reads it in place as its B operand and qk_group reads it one token per lane.
PR 4's per-slot record of the saved K rows of a page (one bit per page offset) and the two functions that set the bits after a row store and after a whole-block store. Not in this PR.

The index map of the VNNI plane: index(token, dim) gives the element position of one value from its token block, dimension step, pair, token column and half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:107-114]. The worked example maps token 37, dimension 70 to element 5226.

detail::k_vnni_access::plane(view), the one route from a VNNI-packed K view to its raw plane address [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:212-219]. It is open to the typed operations of the header, the two score kernels (qk_group and, from this PR, qk_vnni_128x4) and the test-only fill.

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns one 16 KiB VNNI-packed K plane as a 64-byte-aligned bf16 array, and its as_view() is the only source of a view [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:183-204]. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> (T = bf16 or const bf16, the concept k_vnni_element) is the only way to name a plane, and a writable view converts to a read-only one, never back [127, 137-172].

amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, added here: the AMX kernel that computes S = Q x K^T for one dense page whose K is VNNI-packed, with the padded query rows as the A operand and the 16 K panels as the B operand, writing s[4][64] fp32 unscaled scores [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-303; h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:252-268].

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. A VNNI-packed binary then scores every page with the reader qk_group: an AMX-off run of the same layout, not a rollback to the row-major numerics.

A KV head is one key/value head of grouped-query attention, and kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head (4 for qwen3-4b and llama-3.1-8b). A query group is the kv_mul query heads that share one KV head, and the AMX kernels take groups of 4.

The struct holding the two planes K and V of one (storage slot, KV head, page), KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 being the plane count [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2519, 717]. PR 1 made its member k the typed owner k_vnni_tensor for a VNNI slot (k_storage) [2526-2536].

kv_saves_ is the page's per-offset, per-slot count of saved K and V (main-branch code) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2212-2213]. After all KV heads' rows of a token are stored, save_k_impl marks the token with mark_k_complete and, under hardware attention, credits the GOF (credit_gof_save), and after the token loop it counts the latch down once per downstream minibatch [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3126, 3130, 3134-3135].

batch::upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot countdown object that the downstream attention waits on [h/tron/models/common.hpp:1160]. save_k counts it down once per downstream minibatch after all its row stores [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3135].

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, a compile-time constant that is true only for 128-dimension heads and only when the option is on [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:99-102]. In this PR it picks the packer and the kernel at the two AMX sites of self_attention.hpp.
The main branch of the tron repository, the base of PR 1. Code marked 'main' on this page exists there unchanged by the stack.

words.term: main thread / main helpers / run() / run_main_help / TronCpp.hs
words.definition: The main thread runs the generated plugin's run(), which calls save_k, and the main helpers are its helper threads, which run the generated run_main_help [ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:1364, 1420, 2918-2921]. TronCpp.hs is the Haskell generator of the plugins (PR 3 makes run_main_help call save_k with the helper's worker_ix).

words.term: minibatch / batch / items / token_jobs_do_kv / K buffer ks
words.definition: A minibatch (struct batch) is one chunk of a forward pass's token jobs, its items, and token_jobs_do_kv says per job whether it needs KV work [h/tron/models/common.hpp:991, 1083; h/tron/models/model.hpp:1158]. ks is the K buffer of one layer that save_k reads [3079].
A deliberate code change that a test must catch. For this PR: with the kernel's second panel load changed from token block 1 to block 2, the identity case fails at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:275.

words.term: native K view (page::k, kv_block::k_view, k_at, const_native_k_view)
words.definition: The row-major views of a K plane: page::k returns the kv_block's k_view, a [token][element] view, and k_at(i_page) one token's row, all constrained by PR 1 to row-major slots [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1923-1984, 2554-2572]. const_native_k_view is the argument type of qk_rowmajor_128x4.

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 17) that states the gates of the AMX path and its numerics contract: the AMX path differs from the AVX-512 path in the bf16 rounding of the PV weights and in the fp32 add order.

The comment block in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (line 651) that says who writes and who reads the VNNI K layout. This PR rewrites the route sentence of its typed-plane paragraph and its Why paragraph, its consumer items 2 and 3 and its kill-switch paragraph for the kernel [667-675, 683-691, 708-712].

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (lines 195-229) that explains the flipped operand roles: the row-major kernel computes S^T = K x Q^T and transposes in registers, and with VNNI-packed K the kernel computes S = Q x K^T with no transpose. This PR adds its VNNI paragraph [222-229].

PR 3's comment block in model.hpp that records why save_k was the main thread's largest serial piece of a prefill layer with the per-row store (0.86 ms per layer, measured 2026-09-14) and the two remedies: the block save and the sharing with the main helpers. Not in this PR.

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 94) that says a tile store writes 16 rows, so both QK kernels store into an internal buffer and copy only the 4 query rows out. s16 is that buffer in qk_vnni_128x4, 16 rows x 64 fp32 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:247, 296-302].
The CMake option, off by default, that selects VNNI-packed K for every 128-dimension head. It stays off in every build preset until PR 4.

words.term: packers (pack_q_group_128x4, pack_q_rows_128x4) / query pack / query-pack slot (amx_qpack_slot)
words.definition: The packers prepare the queries of one group: pack_q_group_128x4 (main branch) packs the 4 rows into the VNNI layout as the B operand of the row-major kernel, and pack_q_rows_128x4 (this PR) copies the 4 rows as stored into rows 0 to 3 of a 16-row A operand [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:136, 225-229]. A query pack is one packer call for one query token, into a query-pack slot, one 4,096-byte buffer per query token that serves either packer [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:256-263, 1690-1713].

A block of 64 contiguous tokens of KV data (page_size), the unit by which attention proceeds [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1825-1827]. A page struct is a lightweight reference into a book and keeps the per-token save counters.

words.term: page K-state helpers of PR 4 (k_state_ix, k_storage_ref, k_storage_of, eagle_view_active, k_block_bits, k_block_is_vnni, block_bit, offset_bit, k_with_storage_geometry, k_storage_readable)
words.definition: The helpers PR 4 adds around the two bit arrays: which state entry and which storage slot a call means, the bit masks of one block or one offset, the acquire read of a block bit, and whether a storage slot can be read. None exists at this PR.

One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords. The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart, and one pair row is one 64-byte tile row of the kernel's B tile.

The 1 KiB part of a K plane for one 32-dimension step s and one 16-token block c: 16 pair rows of 64 bytes, at index s * 4 + c, 16 per plane [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:25-27, 75-79]. A panel is exactly one AMX B tile, which the kernel's static_asserts check [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:257-267].

words.term: per-row store (store_row, load_row, set_k_row, get_k_row, pair_base, pair_row_offsets)
words.definition: PR 1's way of writing one token's 128-dimension row into the VNNI plane: store_row issues 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, into the token's column of its block's 4 panels, load_row is the inverse gather, and pair_base and pair_row_offsets are their address helpers [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:264-283, 294-306, 313-325]. page::set_k_row and page::get_k_row call them for a VNNI slot and memcpy for a row-major slot, and in this PR save_k stores every row this way [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2040; h/tron/models/model.hpp:3113, 3118].
K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane. For a VNNI slot kv_block::k owns it as a k_vnni_tensor.
A pull request of the tron repository: PR 1 is #4868, PR 2 (this page) is #4887, PR 3 is #4898 and PR 4 is #4901. Each is based on the previous one, and all four replace PR #4424.
The prompt length in tokens of a measurement cell (the runtron flag --prompt-length). Every run then generates 256 tokens.

QK is the score step of attention, S = Q x K^T, done for one dense page by qk_rowmajor_128x4 or qk_vnni_128x4. PV is the weights-times-values step, O = P x V, where P is the exponentiated scores, done by weights_times_v_128x4 [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:270-281].

k_vnni::qk_group, PR 1's AVX-512 routine that scores a query group against one VNNI-packed page, one token per vector lane, for the tokens set in a live mask [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:60-62]. In this PR it serves every page the kernel does not take: partial or partly visible pages, the kill switch, hosts without AMX, builds without AMX dispatch, and the shapes and query types outside the AMX gate.

The AMX QK kernel of main for a row-major K page: K is the A operand and Q is VNNI-packed as the B operand. The result is transposed in AVX-512 registers on the way out [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:156; h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:237].
The 4-billion-parameter model of the PR body's measurements, with kv_mul 4 and 128-dimension heads.

The CI (continuous integration) documentation of tron. This PR adds the paragraph that says the identity case compiles in every AMX-dispatch build and executes AMX only on a Granite Rapids (an Intel CPU generation with AMX) runner [README.ci.md:597-600].
One row of head_size bf16 values per token, the K layout of main and of every head size other than 128 under the option. A row-major slot keeps the native K views and the dotter.

words.term: row-major tail block (row_major_row, store_row_major, load_row_major, k_row_if_row_major)
words.definition: PR 4's form of an incomplete 16-token block of a VNNI slot, none of which exists at this PR: token t owns 256 contiguous bytes until all 16 rows are saved, then the block is converted in place. row_major_row addresses such a row, store_row_major and load_row_major copy it, and page::k_row_if_row_major hands it to the FPGA staging.

save_k (two overloads) stores the K rows of one minibatch for one layer and calls save_k_impl, which at this PR stores every row on the main thread inside its per-token loop, with set_k_row for a VNNI slot and page::k(...).set for a row-major slot [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3077, 3091-3135, 3139, 3147]. save_v_impl and the two save_v overloads are the V counterpart [3155, 3204, 3212].

Q is the query matrix, K the key matrix and S = Q x K^T the score matrix of one query group against the tokens of one page. The AMX kernels write the raw, unscaled scores into s_pages[head][token], 4 rows of 64 fp32, the array the software loop also fills [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1774-1787].

PR 3's whole-block store, none of which exists at this PR: store_block transposes the 16 rows of a block in registers (transpose_16x16_epi32) and writes them as 64 whole lines, page::set_k_block calls it for one KV head, and store_k_block in model.hpp stores one work unit of a minibatch. At PR 3 store_block and page::set_k_block take a 16-bit present mask and store a partial block with masked line stores, and PR 4 removes the mask from page::set_k_block and passes the full mask to store_block.

A slot is one persistent K/V storage region of a book, selected by kv_slot_id [h/tron/attention_ids.hpp:23], and a storage slot (kv_storage_offset) is the absolute offset of such a region in the book's physical allocation [h/tron/models/common.hpp:240]. A VNNI-packed slot is one whose K uses the VNNI layout.
PR 1's unit test of the VNNI K layout, 4 cases [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp]. Its copy_token call is at line 189.

The clause && !k_vnni::layout_on<operation_head_size> that PR 1 placed on the dense AMX page path, sending every page of a VNNI-packed slot to the reader. This PR removes it [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1904-1905].

An AMX register of 16 rows by 64 bytes. begin_region configures all 8 tile registers (N_TILES_8), and the kernels of amx_attn.cpp use 7 of them: accumulators 0 to 3 and operand tiles 4 to 6 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:37-63].

TPS is tokens per second (the decode throughput) and TTFT is the time to first token (the prefill wall time). The PR body's decision band is twice the larger sample standard deviation over 3 repetitions, never smaller than 0.4 TPS or 0.15 s.

PR 1's typed view of one token's 128 bf16 values in dimension order with the caller's alignment and DMA (direct memory access) flags, not VNNI-packed storage [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:222-231]. k_source_row builds a read-only row and k_destination_row a writable one, and the identity case builds its rows with k_source_row [237-256; t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:252].
The lock on the scheduler's token tree. Page clears and copies run between forward passes while it is held, so no forward pass reads the book then.
The inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool.

A compile-time check in t_llama_unit (a requires expression under STATIC_REQUIRE) that the kernel accepts k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> and its writable form, and rejects const bf16*, bf16*, the native K view and the V view [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:103-106, 428-434].
The owner and the typed view of the VNNI-packed V plane of a kv_block, unchanged by the stack [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2541, 2546]. The kernel rejects it as its K argument.

VNNI (Vector Neural Network Instructions) names the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply, in which two consecutive dimensions of one token are adjacent in memory and one 64-byte line holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens. VNNI-packed means stored in this layout.
The example the three source pages trace: token 37, dimension 70 of the K plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7, at element 5226 of the VNNI form (panel #10, pair row 3, dword 5).

what_lands.concept: Note [QK orientation]: the flipped operand roles
what_lands.where: h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:195-229 (the VNNI paragraph at 222-229); Note [AMX attention dispatch] lines 27-29 and its flow chart line 63
what_lands.note: The AMX tile multiply takes a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. With VNNI-packed K the kernel computes S = Q x K^T with Q as A and the 16 K panels as B. The register transpose of the row-major kernel is therefore not needed.

what_lands.concept: The padded query rows: pack_q_rows_128x4 and the shared query-pack slot
what_lands.note: The packer copies the 4 query rows of a group (1 KiB) into rows 0 to 3 of a 16-row A operand whose rows 4 to 15 stay zero. The 4 KiB query-pack slot is the size of the row-major packer's output. One slot therefore serves either packer.

what_lands.concept: The typed boundary: the kernel takes k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> and is the second user of k_vnni_access::plane
what_lands.note: The kernel's K argument is the read-only view that page::k_packed returns, and it reaches the raw plane address only through detail::k_vnni_access::plane. Six compile-time checks pin that the kernel accepts the view and rejects raw pointers, the native K view and the V view.

what_lands.concept: qk_vnni_128x4: the AMX QK kernel on the VNNI plane
what_lands.where: src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:58-63 (the tile names), 231-303 (the kernel); declaration h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:252-268
what_lands.note: The padded Q rows load into tile 4. In each of the 4 dimension steps the panels of token blocks 0 to 3 load into tiles 5 and 6 and multiply into accumulator tiles 0 to 3. The four 16-row tile stores go to the internal buffer s16 and only the 4 query rows are copied out. The scores therefore land as S[query][token] with no transpose.

what_lands.concept: Dispatch by the layout gate: packer and kernel per build, the temporary gate removed, the kill switch
what_lands.note: At the pack site k_vnni::layout_on picks pack_q_rows_128x4 for a VNNI-packed slot, and at the dense-page site it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with page::k_packed. The clause && !k_vnni::layout_on that PR 1 placed on the dense AMX page path is removed, and every other page keeps the reader qk_group. walkthrough.say: Start at the plane: one K plane is 16 panels of 1 KiB, one per (dimension step s, token block c), and a panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes. Point at the panel (s, c) box and the pair row box: a panel is exactly one AMX B tile, and that is the whole reason for the layout. Open src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:257-268, where five static_asserts pin the drawing to the tile, and 279-294, where each tile load takes panel (step * 4 + block). No box of this diagram changes in this PR.

Open Note [QK orientation] at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:195-229: the AMX tile multiply takes a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. Main's kernel therefore computes S^T = K x Q^T with K as A and VNNI-packed Q as B, and transposes the result in registers. With VNNI-packed K the roles flip: Q is A and the panels are B. S = Q x K^T then comes out in the orientation the softmax step (the scaling and exponentiation of the scores in the caller) wants, with no transpose (lines 222-229).

Point at the box amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, the kernel this PR adds, and the route from k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> through detail::k_vnni_access::plane. The kernel's K argument is the type page::k_packed returns (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997), and the one raw-address call is amx_attn.cpp:244. The typed-boundary probe in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:428-434 checks that the kernel accepts the view and rejects raw pointers, the native K view and the V view. The owner, the views and the reader qk_group in this diagram are PR 1.

First the A operand: pack_q_rows_128x4 at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:225-229 is a 1 KiB memcpy of the 4 query rows into rows 0 to 3 of a zeroed 4 KiB query-pack slot (h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:256-263), and rows 4 to 15 stay zero. Now the kernel, 237-303: the padded Q rows load into tile 4 (line 278). In each of the 4 dimension steps the panels of token blocks 0 to 3 load into tiles 5 and 6 and each multiplies into accumulator tile 0 to 3 (279-294). The four 16-row tile stores go to the buffer s16 (296-299) and only rows 0 to 3 are copied out (300-302).

Point at the apply_page_tok / apply_dense_amx_page caller row and the qk_vnni_128x4 cell. Open h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1707-1711 (the layout gate picks the packer) and 1781-1787 (it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with k_packed or qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k). At 1904-1910 the temporary gate clause of PR 1 is gone, and every page the kernel does not take keeps the reader qk_group (1994-1997), as Note [K VNNI storage] items 2 and 3 now say (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:683-694). With the kill switch available() is false (1540) and no query is packed (1634-1636). Every page of a VNNI slot then takes qk_group. The body's forced run shows that newoff (this binary with the kill switch) and head (PR 1's binary) score identically at all 256 steps.

On the lanes, the kernel sits in the attention-worker box next to qk_group: it runs on an attention worker, reads the plane through the same route and writes only its own score buffer (amx_attn.cpp:244, 247). No thread rule changes in this PR. The save_k lanes of PR 3 and the forward-end conversion of PR 4 are not here yet.

Use this diagram to say what is not yet true: at this PR a VNNI slot has one form only. Every row enters through store_row (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2022). The kernel therefore reads all 16 panels with no per-block check (amx_attn.cpp:277-295). The row-major form, the block bit and the k_layout_dense gate are PR 4.

Tests: the identity case in t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:219-279 stores the same K row-major and, through store_row in scrambled token order (249-252), VNNI-packed, packs the same queries both ways (256-257), runs both kernels (263-268) and compares the 4 x 64 fp32 scores bit for bit (275). Both kernels add the same four 32-dimension partial products in the same order inside the tile multiply, whichever operand holds K (the case comment at 221-228). That is why the scores must match bit for bit. The mutation check, the second panel load changed from block 1 to block 2, fails at line 275. The dispatch test counts one pack, one QK and one PV call for a full page under either layout and checks that the packer of the build's layout ran (t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:171, 196).

Close with the numbers of the PR body: decode throughput against main rises by 5.4 % at prompt 1,024 tokens and by 9.5 % at prompt 8,192 tokens (qwen3-4b, 8 users). That recovers the loss PR 1 showed. TTFT against main is +3.2 % at prompt 1,024 tokens (inside the band) and -1.0 % at prompt 8,192 tokens (beyond the band, an improvement). The PR body does not isolate the per-row store's TTFT cost, and PR 3 (#4898) replaces the per-row store with the shared block save. The option stays off in every build preset until PR 4.
